feature: Math.roman(n: number): string is a bespoke (invented) built-in added under the Math namespace, so the static type checker treats it as `any` and no TypeSystem change is needed. It is implemented as an entry method Roman(double) that validates range and drops the fractional part, plus a per-place Tier(...) helper that emits the glyphs for the thousands/hundreds/tens/ones place using a switch on the place digit.
contract: 1. Truncate the argument to an integer (drop the fractional part).
2. Reject out-of-range input: any integer < 1 OR > 3999 maps to the empty string (no Roman representation).

3. For each place value (1000, 100, 10, 1) emit glyphs using classical notation: 0-3 additive (e.g. III), 4 subtractive (one+five, e.g. IV), 5-8 additive on top of five (e.g. VIII), 9 subtractive (one+ten, e.g. IX).
4. Concatenate place outputs from most to least significant. Examples: 4->IV, 9->IX, 40->XL, 90->XC, 444->CDXLIV, 900->CM, 2024->MMXXIV, 3888->MMMDCCCLXXXVIII, 3999->MMMCMXCIX.

BUG_A_nine_form.wrong_code: case 9: sb.Append(five); for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) sb.Append(one); break;
BUG_A_nine_form.effect: The 9 in any place is rendered as five followed by four ones (an additive run) instead of the subtractive one+ten. So 9 -> VIIII (not IX), 90 -> LXXXX (not XC), 900 -> DCCCC (not CM), 3999 -> MMMDCCCCLXXXXVIIII (not MMMCMXCIX).

BUG_B_upper_range_guard.effect: Only the lower bound is checked. Inputs above 3999 are not rejected, so the thousands Tier runs with a digit of 4+ and emits a malformed string (4000 -> 'M\u0000', 5000 -> '\u0000') instead of the empty string. This is the edge a quick fix to the 9-form overlooks: fixing only BUG A still leaves out-of-range input broken.

why_medium: Both symptoms are named in the prompt with concrete examples, so this is a normal two-symptom bug report, not a hidden-bug trap. The genuine gotcha is that the two defects live in different helpers: BUG A is in the per-place switch (Tier), BUG B is in the entry guard (Roman). A solver who patches only the visible 9-form symptom (BUG A) and stops -- or who 'fixes' the range by clamping rather than returning empty -- leaves BUG B failing and scores 10/12 = 0.833, below the 0.9 gate. Fixing both is a small, clean change once both are read.

r10.area: BUG A (9 in three places at once, max value)

partial_fix_traps: Fixing only BUG A (the 9-form) makes r7-r10 pass but leaves r11/r12 (out-of-range) failing -> 10/12 = 0.833, below the 0.9 gate.
Fixing only BUG B (the range guard) makes r11/r12 pass but leaves r7-r10 failing -> 8/12 = 0.667, below the gate.

Both bugs are explicitly described with examples, so a competent solver typically fixes both; the trap only catches a solver who treats the prompt as a single-symptom report and patches just the demonstrated 9 case.
visible: Single repro: Math.roman(9) -> expected 'IX'. Fails in broken (renders 'VIIII'), passes when fixed. Demonstrates BUG A only; the visible suite does not exercise the out-of-range edge.
no_pristine_gold: The feature is newly added by defect.patch, so there is no pristine gold tree; validate with --skip-gold.
